content.title: Has an amateur ever won the Masters? History, results and 2026 field
content.text: Has an amateur ever won the Masters? History, results and 2026 fieldFollow along as USA TODAY Sports provides live coverage and leaderboard updates from the 2026 Masters Tournament.The 2026 Masters Tournament is underway from Augusta National in Georgia, where the world's top players seek to become immortalized by winning on one of the most renowned courses in the history of golf.AdvertisementThat includes a small group of players for whom a win would not only be a massive upset, but also a historic addition to the tournament that claims the moniker, "A Tradition Unlike Any Other."More: 2026 Masters LeaderboardSix players in the field hoping to make the cut line and challenge for what would be a historic first at Augusta: an amateur winning the Masters.Here's what to know about the feat, whether it has ever been achieved, top amateur finishes and what happens should an amateur claim the top of the leaderboard at Augusta.1 / 55See photos from the Masters Par 3 Contest full of kids and smilesOn Wednesday at Augusta National, the Par 3 Contest replaces routine with play, as kids wander onto the greens and smiles outnumber swings before the Masters gets underway.These images capture the lighthearted moments that define the Par 3 Contest each year, when players share the course with their children and the focus shifts from preparation to pure joy.Above, Jordan Spieth and his wife, Annie Verret, crouch down on the ninth green as their son, Sully, crawls across during the Par 3 Contest at the Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club. Spieth’s oldest child, Sammy, clings to his back.2 / 55See photos from the Masters Par 3 Contest full of kids and smilesSergio Garcia's son, Enzo, plays on the third green during the Par 3 Contest at the Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club.55 / 55See photos from the Masters Par 3 Contest full of kids and smilesBernhard Langer walks on the first green during the Par 3 Contest at the Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club.No, an amateur has never won the Masters Tournament, though several golfers have come agonizingly close over the years.AdvertisementOne notable recent example is Sam Bennett, who opened the 2023 Masters Tournament with consecutive rounds of 4-under 68 to sit in third place after 36 holes. He shot a third-round score 76, good enough to become the first amateur to enter the final round still in the top 10 since 1964. He finished Round 4 with a score of 2-over 74 to finish 2-under-par for the tournament and tied for 16th place.It was the best finish by an amateur since Ryan Moore finished tied for 13th in 2005.Best amateur finishes at the MastersHere's a look at some of the top finishes by amateurs in the history of the Masters:Advertisement2nd: Ken Venturi (1956)T-2nd: Frank Stranahan (1947)T-2nd: Charlie Coe (1961)3rd: Billy Joe Patton (1954)4th: Harvie Ward (1957)6th: Charles Coe (1959)T-6th: Lawson Tittle (1935)T-7th: Jack Nicklaus (1961)REQUIRED READING: Meet the 6 amateurs playing in the 2026 Masters at Augusta National2026 amateurs competing at the MastersHere's a look at the 2006 amateur field at the Masters:Jackson HerringtonBrandon HoltzMason HowellMateo PulciniEthan FangFifa LaopakdeeWhat happens if an amateur wins the Masters?Should an amateur win the Masters, they will leave Augusta National with a green jacket and Silver Cup, the latter of which is presented to the low amateur. However, according to the Masters, because of their amateur status, they are unable to earn prize money – even the winner's purse. The money will instead be distributed starting with the second-place golfer-onward.This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Has an amateur ever won Masters? History, results, 2026 field
